squawks.headline: US Federal Maritime Commission proposes a fee on all Spanish vessels
squawks.detail: The US Federal Maritime Commission has proposed charging a fee on every Spanish vessel, according to a market news report. The report gave no figures or timing.

squawks.headline: US gasoline prices jump 9.1% m/m in September, making up more than half of the monthly CPI increase
squawks.detail: BLS data show headline CPI at 3.7% y/y in September, up from 3.4%, and core CPI at 2.6%, up from 2.4%. Gasoline rose 9.1% on the month and made up more than half of the monthly rise in CPI.

squawks.headline: US 2-year Treasury yield extends rise to 12.72bp at 4.92%, its highest since 29 September
squawks.detail: The US 2-year Treasury yield was last up 12.72bp at 4.92%, its highest level since 29 September, after the September US CPI data.

squawks.headline: US supercore CPI rises 0.42% m/m in September, slower than 0.51% the month before
squawks.detail: US supercore CPI rose 0.42% month on month in September, compared with 0.51% in the previous month, according to the September US CPI release.

squawks.headline: US supercore CPI rises to 3.13% y/y in September from 3.02% the month before
squawks.detail: The supercore figure comes from the same US September CPI release, which put headline inflation at 3.7% y/y. The FT reports that higher fuel costs linked to the Iran war pushed prices up.

squawks.headline: US 2-year Treasury yield climbs 10bp to 4.89% and dollar index hits its highest since November after hotter US CPI
squawks.detail: The moves followed September US CPI. Core rose 0.3% m/m against 0.2% expected. Kalshi pricing put the chance of an October Fed hike at 33%, up from 21%, and the Bloomberg dollar spot index rose to its highest since November.

squawks.headline: US September CPI rises to 3.7% y/y, above the 3.6% forecast; core CPI 2.6% y/y; traders add to Fed hike bets
squawks.detail: US headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m in September, in line with forecasts, and 3.7% y/y against 3.4% previously; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m against a 0.2% forecast and 2.6% y/y against a 2.5% forecast. The FT reported that fuel prices rebounded because of the war in Iran; US short-term rate futures fell and traders added to bets on a Fed rate hike in October.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says the European Commission will get a new trade tool so it can respond quickly to developments
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European Commission will have a new trade instrument for responding quickly to developments. The remarks come amid German moves to press the EU on capping additional imports from China.

squawks.headline: Container ship and dry bulk ship reported sinking near Strait of Hormuz after being hit by projectiles
squawks.detail: Maritime security sources say a container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after a projectile hit it, and a dry bulk ship is reported to be sinking after being hit in a separate incident. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Oman, Russia and China are mediating ceasefire talks with the Houthis, an official tells AP
squawks.detail: AP reports an official as saying Oman, Russia and China are mediating ceasefire talks with Yemen's Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi targets including Aramco sites.

squawks.headline: ECB's Simkus says recent data point to a possible need for more tightening, with no clear second-round effects so far
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Simkus said recent data suggest further tightening may be required, and that second-round effects are not yet evident. He added that French yields are rising because of economic developments, that he sees no role for the ECB in France at present, and that discussing minimum reserve requirements is not wrong.

squawks.headline: EU's Dombrovskis says trade with China must be rebalanced in other sectors after the hybrid car deal
squawks.detail: European Economic Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said on Wednesday that the deal to halve Chinese hybrid car imports into Europe must be followed by rebalancing in other sectors and better EU access to the Chinese market, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says first diesel export shipments are under way and exports could reach 3.5m tonnes a month by year-end
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said the first diesel export cargoes are under way and that Russian and US companies are already negotiating contracts for diesel supplies to the US, Tass reported. Tass also reported that Russia could raise diesel exports to 3.5m tonnes a month by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister calls for a ceasefire for civilian shipping in the Black Sea and expects US support for Ukraine to continue
squawks.detail: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany does not see a substantial cut in US support for Ukraine and that the US is right to push for Russia-Ukraine talks. He also called for a ceasefire covering civilian shipping in the Black Sea.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says US diesel deal lets Russia raise output and refining, with supplies going to world markets and the US
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the Russia-US diesel deal gives Russia room to increase its production and refining volumes. He said supplies will go both to global markets and directly to the United States.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says at PMQs that his priority on the Trump-Russia diesel deal is to build bridges, ahead of meeting Zelenskiy
squawks.detail: At Prime Minister's Questions, Prime Minister Burnham was asked about the US-Russia diesel deal and said his job is to bring people back together. He also said Ukraine's President Zelenskiy would not leave their meeting empty-handed.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham pledges to bring down the UK welfare bill
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said on 14 October that the government will reduce welfare spending. He gave no figures or timetable.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim to have driven Saudi forces out of Bab al-Mandab and Dhubab airport
squawks.detail: A Houthi spokesperson says Saudi forces have been expelled from the Bab al-Mandab area and Dhubab airport, with vehicles burned or captured and personnel taken prisoner. The spokesperson says footage will be released at 4 PM on 14 October.

squawks.headline: Putin's envoy Dmitriev says Russia will keep up economic cooperation with the US beyond diesel
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Russia's economic cooperation with the United States would continue and would not be limited to diesel. The remark follows reports that Russia and the US are discussing diesel supply contracts.

squawks.headline: Aramco's Dhahran headquarters reported extensively damaged in Tuesday's attack, though sources say operations continue normally
squawks.detail: According to sources, fire spread across several floors of the Dhahran headquarters. Aramco has told staff to work from home and has moved some operations to its offices abroad, and sources say operations are continuing normally.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams sees no need for further rate hikes in 2027 while markets still price three
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that New York Fed President John Williams does not see a need for more rate hikes in 2027. Markets are still pricing three Fed hikes.

squawks.headline: European Commission warns of a very difficult winter, with high energy prices and an affordability crisis
squawks.detail: A European Commission spokesperson says the EU faces high energy prices, an affordability crisis and a very volatile, unpredictable outlook this winter.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says US diesel contract will include a mechanism to keep supplies flowing despite Western sanctions
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia and the US are negotiating to finalise a diesel contract. He said the contract will include a mechanism to secure supplies despite Western sanctions.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak expects oil output to recover and says OPEC+ capacity assessment report is due late 2026
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak also said the fuel oil market is improving and some Russian refineries have finished maintenance, TASS and Interfax report.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Russia and the US are discussing diesel contracts and a US diesel supply deal is in sight
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak made the remarks, according to TASS and Interfax. Russia remains under sanctions.

squawks.headline: Saudi shares fall after the attack on an Aramco building while other Gulf markets trade mixed
squawks.detail: Reuters reports Saudi stocks fell in early trade on Wednesday after the attack on a Saudi Aramco site added to concerns over the escalating conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Houthis. Other major Gulf markets were mixed.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman says the Fed is planning a full reorganisation to fix the risk-averse culture seen in the SVB collapse
squawks.detail: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said work is under way on a complete reorganisation to address the culture problems that surfaced during the Silicon Valley Bank failure.

squawks.headline: Russia restarts diesel exports from Primorsk after the US temporarily eases sanctions under the Trump deal
squawks.detail: Russia has resumed diesel shipments from its Baltic port of Primorsk, with a 40,000-ton tanker heading to Morocco. Moscow expects its exports to reach 3-3.5 million tons a month by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Fed's Bowman sees no urgency for further rate action and says the Fed can wait and assess conditions
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said there was no immediate need for more moves on rates. She said the Fed could wait and assess conditions before acting again.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says the terms of Trump's proposed energy ceasefire have not been set out and work is continuing
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the provisions of the energy ceasefire proposed by the US president remain unclear and that work on it is in progress. It also accused European countries of acting to prolong the war in Ukraine while US negotiators pursue a peace settlement.

squawks.headline: Israel's Netanyahu says he opposes a pre-emptive attack on Iran for now, ahead of the elections, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say the Israeli prime minister told IDF Radio that a pre-emptive strike on Iran before the elections would not suit Israel at present. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: German 30-year Bund auction yields 3.8% with bid-to-cover of 1.4, down from 1.6 last time
squawks.detail: Germany's 30-year Bund auction has an average yield of 3.8%, the same as at the previous sale. Its bid-to-cover ratio is 1.4, compared with 1.6 last time.

squawks.headline: IEA says tight diesel supplies could last well into 2027
squawks.detail: In its monthly oil market report, the International Energy Agency said diesel shortages could last well into next year. It said large stock drawdowns at a time of year when stocks usually build, together with limited production, come just before peak winter demand.

squawks.headline: UK 4-year gilt auction yields 4.945% with bid-to-cover of 3.415
squawks.detail: The 4-year gilt auction had an average yield of 4.945%, up from 4.786% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 3.415, compared with 3.237 last time.

squawks.headline: Trump is considering revisiting US intelligence sharing with Ukraine, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the White House is actively discussing intelligence sharing with Ukraine. It says CIA Director Ratcliffe is opposed to halting it.

squawks.headline: China buys 8-10 US soybean cargoes, its first such deals since the Trump-Xi summit, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Chinese state buyers bought 8-10 Panamax cargoes of US soybeans this week, three trade sources told Reuters. These are the first such purchases since the September summit in Washington between Presidents Trump and Xi.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco in Dhahran, a Riyadh Aramco refinery and King Khalid Airport, and say attacks will continue
squawks.detail: A Houthi military spokesperson said the group targeted Aramco facilities in Dhahran, an Aramco refinery in Riyadh and King Khalid Airport. The group said its operations against airports and oil facilities will continue in the coming days.

squawks.headline: European Commission proposes delaying EU methane rules on imported oil and gas by one year
squawks.detail: The European Commission has proposed postponing by one year the EU methane emissions rules that apply to imported oil and gas.

squawks.headline: IFS launches its Green Budget 2026 ahead of the Budget
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies began its live launch of the Green Budget 2026 on Wednesday morning, with presentations from IFS authors and Barclays. The report is funded by the Nuffield Foundation.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthi forces say they will announce a military operation deep inside Saudi territory
squawks.detail: Houthi armed forces say they will announce a 'qualitative' military operation deep inside Saudi Arabia at 11:40 AM. The statement follows Tuesday's Houthi attacks, which included a reported hit on Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters.

squawks.headline: German economy ministry sees little short-term support from domestic demand and a subdued industrial outlook
squawks.detail: Germany's economy ministry says weaker purchasing power from higher energy prices, uncertainty and financing costs mean the domestic economy is unlikely to add much momentum in the short term. It also says the outlook for industrial activity remains subdued.

squawks.headline: German economy ministry says the economy's momentum probably slowed temporarily in the third quarter
squawks.detail: Germany's economy ministry gave the assessment in its monthly report, published on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: ECB's Elderson says banks and supervisors must look beyond data-driven models to deal with non-linear climate and nature risks
squawks.detail: The ECB Executive Board member called for scenario analysis and stronger risk management frameworks. He said uncertainty also comes from demographics, AI and quantum computing.

squawks.headline: IEA now sees 2026 world oil demand down 2.6m bpd and supply down 5.8m bpd, both slightly steeper than it forecast before
squawks.detail: In its monthly report, the IEA put 2026 supply at 1.73m bpd below demand (previously 1.74m bpd) and sees 2027 supply 3.94m bpd above demand (previously 3.73m bpd), citing disruption from the Iran war and very high prices. It said tight middle distillate supply will last well into 2027 and that the latest wave of attacks puts September's recovery in Middle East oil exports at risk.

squawks.headline: Germany plans to press the EU to cap additional imports from China
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that Germany will push the EU to put caps on additional Chinese imports. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Italy's Meloni calls the US-Russia diesel deal very risky and says the EU needs a seat in Russia-Ukraine talks
squawks.detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the US-Russia diesel deal works against efforts to bring Putin to the negotiating table with Ukraine. She also said the EU needs a representative in negotiations on the war.

squawks.headline: Italy's Meloni says a deal with the EU on limiting the effect of gas costs on electricity prices is close
squawks.detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Italy sees an agreement with the EU nearing on measures to reduce how much gas costs feed through to electricity prices. No details of the measures or timing were given.

squawks.headline: Eurozone bond yields fall ahead of US CPI data and bond auctions
squawks.detail: Eurozone government bond yields were reported lower on Wednesday morning, ahead of the US CPI release and upcoming auctions. No figures were given for the size of the move.

squawks.headline: Oman says Hormuz discussions cannot be completed without US-Iran talks
squawks.detail: Oman said that whether discussions on the Strait of Hormuz can be completed depends on talks between the US and Iran.

squawks.headline: Oil prices rise on Wednesday after two vessels are hit in Hormuz and Iran says it is using new tactics against shipping
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two ships were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials said they were using new tactics to target vessels. No size for the price move was given.

squawks.headline: India's September wholesale price inflation climbs to 11.39% y/y, above the 10.60% forecast
squawks.detail: India's wholesale price index rose 11.39% y/y in September, up from 9.92% in August and above the 10.60% estimate. The output PPI also rose 11.39% y/y, up from 9.81% previously.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill says markets may be overpricing the chance of four rate hikes in the next 12 months
squawks.detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said market pricing of four rate increases over the coming 12 months may be overdone. No market reaction was reported in the input.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Russia's latest attack shows Moscow does not take the US president's statements seriously
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president made the comment after a Russian attack, as the US pushes Moscow to join an energy ceasefire.

squawks.headline: German wholesale prices rise 8.7% y/y in September, up from 6.8% in August
squawks.detail: German wholesale prices rose 1.9% m/m in September, compared with 0.9% the previous month. The annual rate climbed to 8.7% from 6.8%.

squawks.headline: Swedish CPI holds at 1.1% y/y in September, in line with forecasts; CPIF steady at 1.5%
squawks.detail: Swedish CPI and CPIF both rose 0.9% m/m, matching estimates. CPIF excluding energy was 0.5% y/y, and household consumption growth slowed to 3.5% y/y from 4.0%.

squawks.headline: Japanese banks and insurers return to domestic bonds as JGB yields surge, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that Japanese banks and insurers are buying domestic government bonds again as yields climb. Investors are watching for signs that Japanese institutions are starting to bring capital home from overseas.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says the US cannot rely on growth to reduce its debt and needs further fiscal adjustment
squawks.detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday that US growth alone will not shrink mounting public debt, and that other fiscal measures are needed to put it on a more sustainable path, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says the ECB focuses on inflation and stays out of individual countries' fiscal matters
squawks.detail: Asked about the French budget, ECB official Moulin said the central bank concentrates on inflation and does not get involved in the fiscal affairs of specific member states.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey is set to pay for Budget giveaways without extra borrowing, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey plans to fund the giveaways in the upcoming Budget without adding to government borrowing.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says Middle East conflict and energy are the main drivers of inflation and expectations remain well anchored
squawks.detail: The Bank of France governor said higher yields may weigh on demand and call for a more moderate policy response to the inflation shock. He also said France must urgently show it is committed to fiscal consolidation and pass its 2027 budget.

squawks.headline: ECB's Wunsch says the ECB is likely to raise interest rates again
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Wunsch said a further ECB rate rise is likely.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says UK debt-curbing steps have improved growth prospects and many countries may need a cautiously hawkish policy stance
squawks.detail: At a press conference in Bangkok, the IMF Managing Director said advanced economies have done worst at rebuilding buffers since the pandemic and that debt-service costs are rising as interest rates go up. She also pointed to rising yields across the euro area, said countries can still borrow in markets but at higher cost, and called for further fiscal adjustment in the US.

squawks.headline: China's September crude imports slip to 37.10m tonnes from 37.93m tonnes in August
squawks.detail: Chinese customs data show January to September crude imports of 357.97m tonnes, down from 422.61m tonnes a year earlier. September natural gas imports rose to 10.86m tonnes from 10.33m tonnes in August.

squawks.headline: China's September exports rise 36.3% y/y in dollar terms, beating the 25.5% poll; trade surplus is $133.53bn
squawks.detail: Chinese customs data show a September trade surplus of $133.53bn against a poll estimate of $118.1bn, including a $34.01bn surplus with the US. The customs vice minister said the export outlook for the fourth quarter is unchanged.

squawks.headline: IMF does not recommend that the UK speed up its fiscal consolidation
squawks.detail: The IMF said it is not recommending that the UK accelerate its fiscal consolidation efforts. Earlier, the IMF had urged advanced economies to cut deficits and debt urgently.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB must act before risks fully emerge and is watching wage bargaining for early signals
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said policymakers are monitoring collective bargaining for early signs of wage growth, that France's debt problems must be addressed mainly through French fiscal policy, and that 1.1% eurozone growth in 2026 is not bad. She also said she has no plans to run for the French presidency.

squawks.headline: Singapore's central bank leaves monetary policy unchanged, against analysts' expectations
squawks.detail: The Monetary Authority of Singapore kept its settings on hold on Wednesday and expects growth and inflation to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says energy explains most but not all of the rise in inflation and second-round effects have not emerged so far
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said the ECB cannot wait for signals to become obvious and is monitoring the wage increases expected through collective bargaining in Europe.

squawks.headline: IMF urges advanced economies to cut deficits and debt urgently, citing higher bond yields and rising debt-service costs
squawks.detail: The IMF warned that delaying fiscal consolidation would make it harder and called on countries to strengthen their public finances before markets force them to. An IMF official also said a combination of corporate, inheritance and capital gains taxes could be preferable to a wealth tax.

squawks.headline: China's September exports rise 29.6% y/y and imports 24.6% y/y in yuan terms, with goods trade topping CNY5tn for the first time
squawks.detail: Chinese customs data show September goods trade of CNY5.16 trillion, up 27.5% y/y. Exports were CNY3.03 trillion and imports CNY2.13 trillion; January to September exports rose 16.4% and imports 22.3%. The customs vice minister said geopolitical conflicts and other global uncertainties cloud the full-year outlook.

squawks.headline: China's September CPI rises 0.9% y/y, below the 1.0% poll, while PPI climbs 5.0% y/y, above forecasts
squawks.detail: China's CPI rose 0.2% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, with core CPI unchanged at 1.0% y/y. PPI rose 5.0% y/y against forecasts of 4.4% to 4.5% and a previous 3.8%, and rose 1.2% m/m.

squawks.headline: Deloitte survey finds large UK firms expect inflation and interest rates to rise over the next year
squawks.detail: The Deloitte survey, published on Wednesday, found big British companies are focusing more on cutting costs. It comes two weeks before Chancellor John Healey's first Budget.

squawks.headline: Iran is using new tactics to step up attacks on Hormuz shipping before the US midterms, senior Iranian officials say
squawks.detail: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Iran aims to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections by targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey plans to make online marketplaces collect tax owed by sellers on their platforms, Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reported that the government plans to make platforms such as Amazon, eBay and Temu responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling through them, as part of a tax crackdown.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says UK companies are concentrating hard on holding down costs as Iran war lifts energy prices
squawks.detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said British firms are focusing closely on containing costs during the energy price surge caused by the Iran war, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: Fed Governor Cook's lawyer challenges Trump's latest attempt to remove her and questions the White House probe
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that a letter from Fed Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer, seen on Tuesday, disputes the objectivity of a White House investigation into mortgage fraud allegations against her. The letter responds to President Trump's latest attempt to remove her from the Fed.

squawks.headline: Saudi energy ministry says the attack on an Aramco building in Dhahran caused a limited fire and no casualties
squawks.detail: Saudi state news agency, citing an energy ministry official, says Tuesday's attack on the Aramco building in Dhahran caused a limited fire and no casualties.

squawks.headline: UK plans fresh Russia sanctions and more support for Ukraine to push Moscow into joining Trump's energy ceasefire
squawks.detail: The UK is reported to be seeking to pressure Russia into joining the energy ceasefire proposed by Trump, with new sanctions on Russia and increased support for Ukraine planned.

squawks.headline: Houthi official threatens new attacks on Saudi oil and other key installations tonight
squawks.detail: In a post on X, a Houthi official said Saudi oil and vital installations would be targeted tonight, following Tuesday's attacks on Dhahran.

squawks.headline: US retail diesel averages $6.28 a gallon on Tuesday, little changed after Trump's Russia diesel announcement
squawks.detail: US retail diesel prices averaged $6.28 per gallon on Tuesday, slightly above Friday's level and below September's record of $6.53 per gallon. The figure shows the announcement has had limited immediate effect on prices.

squawks.headline: Israeli TV reports no intelligence change justifying an Israeli-US move against Iran in the coming weeks
squawks.detail: Israel's N12 News reports that Israel, the US and Gulf states are coordinating and preparing for a range of scenarios, but that no intelligence change justifies a joint Israeli-US move in the coming weeks. The channel also reports that Iran has carried out several ballistic missile tests in recent days, which the Israeli army describes as a slow and only partial restoration of its missile capability.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins says the Fed is not rethinking its 2% inflation target and its models take account of government debt levels
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Collins says the Fed is not reconsidering its 2% inflation target. She also says the Fed's economic models take account of government debt levels.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM says US forces helped Gulf partners move more than 19 million barrels of crude through the strait yesterday
squawks.detail: US Central Command says US forces helped Gulf partners ship more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the strait on Monday.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco headquarters is evacuated after missile attacks from Yemen, Iranian media report
squawks.detail: Iranian media report that Saudi Aramco's headquarters was evacuated after missile attacks launched from Yemen. This follows earlier reports on Tuesday that the Dhahran headquarters had been hit.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins says officials know that higher rates can cause difficulties
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Collins said policymakers are aware that higher interest rates can create challenges. She made the remark in further comments on Tuesday.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran is reported hit during Tuesday's Houthi attacks
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters was hit during Tuesday's Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The reports came after earlier accounts of explosions near the site. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins says economic uncertainty is elevated
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said in further remarks that the level of economic uncertainty is elevated.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins says she is watching how broad inflation pressures are in the data and takes a holistic view of the economy
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she is looking at the economy as a whole when considering the future path of rate policy, and is monitoring the breadth of inflation pressures in incoming data.

squawks.headline: US Treasury's OFAC agrees $11.66m settlement with Bank of America over 475 apparent sanctions violations
squawks.detail: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said on its website that Bank of America is settling potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations. The violations relate to sanctions programmes covering Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia and narcotics.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey backs Warsh's view that forward guidance went too far and notes the UK's budget profile shows a falling deficit
squawks.detail: In further remarks on Tuesday evening, Bank of England Governor Bailey also said leveraged finance is now far more widespread. He repeated that the energy shock gets harder to handle the longer it lasts.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says second-round inflation effects in the UK have been subdued so far but get harder the longer the shock lasts
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said second-round effects have so far been subdued in the UK. He added that the longer an inflation hit persists, the harder it becomes to deal with.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins expects the Fed to raise rates a bit further by year-end and says she backed the September hike
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said tighter policy will help return inflation to 2% and that the path of policy in the new year will depend on the data. She described the US job market as broadly balanced, said the economy has been resilient to shocks and said the data-centre build-out is adding pressure to inflation readings.

squawks.headline: RBNZ is to start buying back April 2027 New Zealand government bonds
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand will begin repurchases of the April 2027 government bond.

squawks.headline: US Treasury fines Bank of America $1.2bn over money laundering and sanctions failures, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the US Treasury fined Bank of America for money laundering and sanctions violations after concluding it did not properly report more than $5bn of suspicious transactions. One report puts the fine at $1.2bn.

squawks.headline: Fed's Collins says elevated inflation risk is the Fed's main focus and expects inflation to stay above 2% on high energy prices
squawks.detail: Boston Fed President Collins said the risk of high inflation is the Fed's main focus at present and that she expects inflation to remain above 2% because of high energy prices. She said the path of policy in the new year will depend on the data.

squawks.headline: IMF cuts its 2026 Gulf growth forecasts and now sees Middle East and North Africa as the only region to shrink this year
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that the IMF has lowered its 2026 growth forecasts across the Gulf states.

squawks.headline: Trump accuses Iran-backed Houthis of deliberately trying to push up oil prices before the US midterms
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports Trump's accusation alongside its report of Saudi-led coalition strikes on Houthi targets in Sanaa.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three missiles and two drones over Riyadh and the southern region
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three missiles and two drones in the Riyadh region and the south of the kingdom. This follows the Houthi warning that any attack on Sanaa would bring a response against Riyadh.

squawks.headline: UKMTO reports a container ship and a tanker hit by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz in two separate incidents
squawks.detail: UKMTO said a verified source reported a container ship hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, then received a further report of a tanker being struck there minutes later. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham and the Chancellor hold roundtables with business leaders, giving reassurance on tax ahead of the Budget
squawks.detail: The prime minister and the chancellor hosted roundtable meetings with senior business figures ahead of the Budget, with Burnham presenting himself as pro-business on tax, the FT reports. No specific measures were reported.

squawks.headline: Iranian crude exports remain at zero in October under the US blockade, Vortexa data shows
squawks.detail: Energy intelligence platform Vortexa says Iran's crude exports have stayed at zero in October after falling sharply in the second week of September, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence says the threat to Riyadh has passed after the earlier aerial threat warning
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence says the danger over Riyadh has lifted. This follows its earlier warning of an aerial threat to the capital during Houthi missile attacks on the kingdom.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Dhahran and Dammam; Saudi Arabia warns of aerial threat to Riyadh
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Dhahran and Dammam in the Eastern Province, and that interception debris fell on a residential area in Dhahran. Saudi Arabia separately warned of a possible hostile aerial threat to Riyadh.

squawks.headline: Loud explosions reported in Dhahran near Saudi Aramco headquarters, according to six sources
squawks.detail: Six sources report hearing loud explosions in Dhahran, close to Saudi Aramco's headquarters. The cause has not been confirmed, and no market reaction has been reported so far.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says AI's potential to replace some workers could weaken their bargaining power and moderate wage growth
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the possibility of AI displacing some workers may reduce their bargaining power, which could moderate wage growth. The remarks follow his earlier comments on long-term interest rates.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says a rise in long-term interest rates amounts to a material tightening relevant to policy setting
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said higher long-term rates represent a material tightening of conditions, which the ECB takes into account when setting its policy stance.

squawks.headline: Saudi statement says the danger in the Eastern Province has passed
squawks.detail: A Saudi statement says the danger in the kingdom's Eastern Province is over. It follows an earlier civil defence warning of possible danger in the region and Houthi threats against Saudi Aramco facilities. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says one more rate hike this year is appropriate but sees no need for a hike in 2027 at this stage
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said the September hike was rooted in risk management, that the economy is not overheating, and that disinflationary forces are still at work. He said the labour market is not adding to inflation, he sees no broad price pressure beyond AI and energy, and AI is the inflation driver he is watching most closely.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says economic shocks are clearly still coming
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin made the remark at an event at Howard University, which has now ended. He also said again that acting on inflation makes sense.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says inflation is clearly proving persistent and that taking action makes sense
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said US inflation is clearly enduring and that it makes sense to act. This follows his earlier remarks on AI investment and on reaching the 2% target.

squawks.headline: Iran threatens to reconsider its relations with the UK and asks for evidence linking it to the Fairford incident
squawks.detail: Iran's Fars news agency reports that Tehran has threatened to seriously reconsider its ties with the UK. Iran has also asked the UK for evidence of any Iranian links to the suspected plot against RAF Fairford.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence warns of possible danger in the Eastern Province
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority has issued an alert about possible danger in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The alert follows Houthi statements that Saudi Aramco facilities are legitimate targets. It gave no further details.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition confirms it struck an oil facility in Sanaa it says the Houthis used to support their attacks
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it attacked the site because the Houthis used it to support drones and missiles that threaten Saudi Arabia and Red Sea ports and shipping. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says the effect of AI investment can be seen in US inflation
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the impact of AI investment is visible in US inflation, according to remarks reported on Tuesday.

squawks.headline: Iran's acting oil minister says South Pars gas capacity is coming back faster
squawks.detail: Iran's acting oil minister said capacity at the South Pars gas field is returning at a faster pace, Mehr News reports. This follows earlier Iranian reports that major repairs to war damage at the field had been finished.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu's office denies he is urging Trump to attack Iran before the elections
squawks.detail: Israel's N12 News reports that the Israeli prime minister's office has denied claims that Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike Iran before the elections. The same outlet quotes a US official as saying Washington is continuing to increase pressure on Iran.

squawks.headline: IRGC says missiles fired from Iranian islands towards ships it calls offending vessels in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say missiles were fired from Iranian islands towards ships in the Strait of Hormuz that they described as offending. This follows an earlier IRGC Navy threat to sink US ships approaching the strait. The post did not report any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran summons UK ambassador over claims linking Tehran to a suspected plot against RAF Fairford
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign ministry says it summoned the UK ambassador over accusations that Tehran was linked to a suspected plot against the Fairford air base in Britain.

squawks.headline: OPEC+ oil output rises sharply in September, led by Saudi Arabia, despite Hormuz disruption
squawks.detail: OPEC reported on Tuesday a sharp gain in OPEC+ production in September, driven by higher Saudi output, even though the Iran war continues to disrupt shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. No aggregate figure was given in the report.

squawks.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine has sent the US proposals for further talks and is ready to meet in the coming days
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said his team has sent the US side proposals for possible next meetings and further talks.

squawks.headline: IRGC Navy commander threatens to sink US ships that approach the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian reports say
squawks.detail: Iranian reports quote Rear Admiral Azmaei, commander of the IRGC Navy, as saying Iran is waiting for American ships to approach the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz so that it can sink them. He also challenged the US to come closer if it believes the strait is open.

squawks.headline: Houthi political council head says Bab al-Mandeb shipping is safe and calls an end to Saudi attacks the easiest solution
squawks.detail: Fars News reports that Mahdi al-Mashat, chairman of Yemen's Houthi-run Supreme Political Council, said shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait is safe and the Houthis are meeting their international obligations. In separate reported remarks, he said the easiest way to resolve the crisis is for Saudi Arabia to end its attacks on Yemen and its siege.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says the 2% inflation target can be reached
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said in remarks on Tuesday that the 2% inflation goal can be hit.

squawks.headline: US VP Vance says the Defense Production Act is being used to expand a Texas refinery
squawks.detail: US Vice President Vance said the administration is using the Defense Production Act to expand refining capacity in Texas. No further details were given in the report.

squawks.headline: US EPA proposes making larger refiners blend more biofuels over the next two years
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the US Environmental Protection Agency on Tuesday proposed fully reallocating refinery biofuel exemptions, which would require larger refiners to blend more biofuels over the next two years.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu discussed possibly resuming the war on Iran with Trump last week, Israeli TV reports
squawks.detail: Israel's N12 News reports that Netanyahu and Trump spoke last week about possibly resuming the war against Iran. It also reports that senior US officials were impressed by Netanyahu's apparent interest in resuming attacks before the elections.

squawks.headline: Fitch says fiscal paths of Western European sovereigns are still diverging
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings published a commentary saying that the fiscal trajectories of Western European sovereigns are continuing to diverge. The post did not give any country-level figures.

squawks.headline: Trump says Yemen's Houthis are behaving very badly as fallout from the US-Iran war spreads across the region
squawks.detail: Reuters reported that US President Trump made the comments about the Houthi militants who control much of Yemen on Tuesday. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says he spoke to the Saudi crown prince, may ask Turkey to join a Yemen response and will decide on Iran soon
squawks.detail: Speaking to reporters, the US president criticised the Houthis' conduct but would not say whether he had made a decision on them, and said a decision on Iran would come very soon. He also said the US is working with Russia and Ukraine to end the war and will say later whether Russia broke the ceasefire.

squawks.headline: Trump says diesel from the Russia deal will go to the world market rather than to the US
squawks.detail: The US president made the remarks about the US-Russia diesel deal. Separately, Republican senators are reported to be urging him to withdraw from the Russian oil deal.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US has not stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine
squawks.detail: The US president said the US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine and wants the war to end. Earlier, Ukraine's president had said intelligence support from partners stopped during overnight attacks.

squawks.headline: US 6-month bills sell at 4.2% and 3-month bills at 4.085%, both higher than the previous auctions
squawks.detail: The US sold $82bn of 6-month bills at a high yield of 4.2%, against 4.165% previously, with bid-to-cover of 2.76 against 2.79. It also sold $95bn of 3-month bills at 4.085%, against 4.05%, with bid-to-cover of 2.68 against 2.51.

squawks.headline: Pimco's Ivascyn says US Treasury yields have not yet peaked and sees the Fed holding this month, with 1 to 2 more hikes this cycle
squawks.detail: Pimco's chief investment officer Dan Ivascyn also said long-dated Treasuries can absorb further Fed tightening. He said spillover risks are greatest in rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and commercial real estate.

squawks.headline: India's foreign minister says Indian and US officials are resolving issues in trade deal talks and progress is positive
squawks.detail: India's external affairs minister said Indian and US officials are working through outstanding issues in their trade deal negotiations, which he described as moving in the right direction.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are set to rise again in January
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the increase will come in the first quarter, when 46% of domestic gas use takes place.

squawks.headline: Saudi cabinet, chaired by the crown prince, says the Houthis will face consequences for repeated attacks on the kingdom
squawks.detail: Saudi state news agency reports the cabinet statement after the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia. No market reaction is reported.

squawks.headline: UK defence secretary Streeting says the MoD must end its culture of overspending and live within its means
squawks.detail: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the Ministry of Defence cannot have a culture of overspending and has a responsibility to stay within its budget. No specific spending measures were announced.

squawks.headline: US existing home sales come in at 3.99m, above the 3.95m forecast
squawks.detail: US existing home sales were 3.99m, against a forecast of 3.95m. The previous reading of 3.98m was revised to 3.93m.

squawks.headline: Warplanes reportedly strike oil company facilities west of Sanaa; Houthis say they are fighting Saudi forces attacking the capital
squawks.detail: Reports say warplanes bombed oil company facilities west of Sanaa, following the Saudi-led coalition's evacuation warning. The Houthis say their forces are confronting Saudi attacks on the Yemeni capital.

squawks.headline: Explosions reported in Sanaa after Saudi-led coalition warning; Houthis say the targeted oil company station holds no fuel
squawks.detail: There are reports of explosions in Sanaa, Yemen. They follow the Saudi-led coalition's order for civilians to evacuate a Yemeni Oil Company site. The Houthis cited an oil company source as saying its As Sabah station is empty of petroleum products and has no military value.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK 10-year gilt yields are the highest among rich countries
squawks.detail: In its Budget preview, the Resolution Foundation said this year's global rise in borrowing costs has also hit the UK. It said UK 10-year government bond yields are now the highest of any rich country.

squawks.headline: Fitch says the jump in bond yields adds to the strain on developed market public finances
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings said the surge in government bond yields makes the challenges facing developed market public finances harder. No figures were given in the report.

squawks.headline: Zelensky says intelligence support from partners has stopped during overnight attacks on Ukraine
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said intelligence support from partners has stopped while night-time attacks continue. Earlier, Ukraine's foreign minister had said intelligence sharing with the US was continuing, and the Kremlin said it knew nothing of a reported Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will also reduce fiscal headroom at the upcoming Budget
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will also eat into the Chancellor's fiscal headroom at the forthcoming Budget. The point comes from its Budget preview, which put the headroom at £12bn, half its previous level.

squawks.headline: Retailers urge Chancellor Healey to cut high street taxes at Downing Street meeting; no Budget measures confirmed
squawks.detail: City AM reports that bosses from Tesco, Sainsbury's and Marks & Spencer pressed the Chancellor on business rates and youth unemployment at a meeting on Tuesday. The Chancellor did not confirm any Budget measures.

squawks.headline: Houthis declare Saudi Aramco facilities legitimate targets and tell nearby workers and residents to evacuate
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi armed forces told employees and civilians near any Saudi Aramco oil facility to leave the area, saying the sites are legitimate targets for their forces. Separately, the US issued a notice advising its citizens to reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia.

squawks.headline: Turkey's Erdogan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in a call with the Saudi crown prince and pledges support
squawks.detail: The Turkish presidency says President Erdogan told the Saudi crown prince by phone that Turkey condemns the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the strongest terms. He also said Turkey will keep standing by Saudi Arabia.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition names Yemeni Oil Company site in Sanaa as the location civilians must evacuate
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition's Joint Forces Command asked civilians to leave the Yemeni Oil Company site at Al-Sabaha Central Station in Sanaa, citing their safety. This follows the coalition's earlier statement that it would soon issue an evacuation call ahead of a special operation.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly data shows private employers added an average of 24,750 jobs a week in the four weeks to 26 September
squawks.detail: ADP's weekly employment measure showed an average gain of 24,750 US private-sector jobs a week in the four weeks to 26 September, up from 23,750 in the previous reading.

squawks.headline: Houthis warn Saudi Arabia that any attack on Sanaa will bring a harsh response against Riyadh
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for Yemen's Houthis said any Saudi strike on the capital, Sanaa, would be met with retaliation against the Saudi capital, Riyadh. The warning follows the Saudi-led coalition's statement that it will soon tell civilians to evacuate a site in Sanaa.

squawks.headline: Hassett says the market trusts the new Fed chair and a slowdown in inflation could give the Fed a reason to hold
squawks.detail: Kevin Hassett said markets have confidence in the incoming Fed chair. He also said the Fed may treat slowing inflation as grounds for holding rates.

squawks.headline: BoK's Shin says policy will stay restrictive until the bank is confident inflation will return to its 2% target
squawks.detail: Bank of Korea Governor Hyun Song Shin welcomed further gains in the won, saying they would support household purchasing power. He said policy will remain restrictive until the bank is confident inflation is heading back to 2%.

squawks.headline: Argentina asks an international tribunal for provisional measures to stop the UK exploiting hydrocarbons off the Falklands
squawks.detail: In a statement, Argentina's government said it had asked an international tribunal for provisional measures to stop the UK exploiting hydrocarbons on a continental shelf around the Falklands. The move follows reports that the UK energy secretary has approved drilling off the islands.

squawks.headline: Iran's oil ministry says it has finished major repairs to war damage at the South Pars gas field, according to reports from Iran
squawks.detail: Reports from Iran attribute the statement to the head of the oil ministry. They say the major repairs to war damage at the South Pars gas field are complete.

squawks.headline: OPEC lifts 2027 oil demand growth forecast to 2.55m bpd and cuts its 2026 forecast to 180,000 bpd
squawks.detail: In its monthly report, OPEC raised its 2027 forecast for global oil demand growth to 2.55 million bpd from 2.36 million bpd. It cut the 2026 forecast to 180,000 bpd from 380,000 bpd.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia tells OPEC its crude output rose to 8.372m bpd in September, recovering from a three-decade low
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that it produced 8.372 million bpd of crude in September, up from 6.238 million bpd in August. OPEC said OPEC+ crude output, including former member UAE, averaged 39.07 million bpd in September, up about 900,000 bpd from August.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition says it will soon tell civilians to evacuate a site in Sanaa, Yemen, ahead of a special operation
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said civilians at a site in the Yemeni capital Sanaa would shortly be warned to evacuate ahead of a planned special operation. The warning follows the Houthis' attack on Saudi Arabia. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK growth beat forecasts in the first half of 2026 but the Middle East conflict has worsened the near-term…
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation made the point in material from its Budget preview. It said UK growth in the first half of 2026 came in ahead of forecasts, and that the Middle East conflict has weakened the short-term outlook.

squawks.headline: Russia's Putin and UAE president discuss the US diesel deal by phone
squawks.detail: Putin held a phone call with the President of the UAE in which they covered the diesel deal with the US, bilateral cooperation and peace in the Middle East.

squawks.headline: Retrofit industry warns over reported plan to cut heat pump subsidies to fund defence in the autumn Budget
squawks.detail: Inside Housing reports that retrofit industry leaders have warned of serious harm to households after reports that the government could reduce heat pump subsidies in the autumn Budget to pay for defence spending.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee voices concern that tariffs and oil prices could lead to stagflation
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said he is concerned that tariffs and oil could produce stagflation, according to a newswire headline. This adds to his earlier remarks on Tuesday about inflation and the Fed's rate path.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says inflation must show progress before the Fed can return to its earlier rate-cutting path
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told Semafor that the Fed needs to see some progress before it can resume the rate-cutting path it had been on. In the same interview he said the AI boom is beginning to push prices up.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says AI is an inflation problem, Semafor reports
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described AI as a source of inflation pressure, according to Semafor.

squawks.headline: UK energy secretary Miliband approves drilling off the Falklands, Telegraph reports
squawks.detail: The Telegraph reports that the energy secretary has given approval for drilling in waters off the Falkland Islands.

squawks.headline: NIESR analysis says UK long-term gilt yields are likely to stay elevated near 5% even if the Iran war ends soon
squawks.detail: The National Institute of Economic and Social Research has published a Market Anatomy report on this year's rise in gilt yields. It says higher borrowing costs are likely to persist, leaving the UK public finances more exposed.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz calls for an immediate end to Iranian and Houthi naval blockades after a call with Saudi crown prince
squawks.detail: The German government said Chancellor Merz spoke by phone with the Saudi crown prince about Houthi attacks, including on Riyadh airport, the Middle East situation and the effect on energy prices. The statement also said Iran must enter serious negotiations and stop destabilising the region.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the Chancellor's fiscal headroom has halved to £12bn ahead of the Budget
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation published new analysis estimating that headroom has halved to £12 billion. It says the Chancellor must weigh support for struggling families against rebuilding confidence in the public finances at the Budget.

squawks.headline: Brent and WTI crude futures drop 2%
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that Brent and WTI crude futures are both down 2% in Tuesday morning trade in Europe. No price levels were given.

squawks.headline: BofA October fund manager survey names a disorderly rise in bond yields as the biggest tail risk to markets
squawks.detail: In BofA's October Fund Manager Survey, investors rank a disorderly rise in bond yields as the top tail risk, ahead of an AI bubble. They say a 5.9% 10-year Treasury yield would lead them to shift allocation from stocks to bonds, and a net 1% expect high long-term rates. A net 4% now expect the global economy to weaken over the next 12 months.

squawks.headline: US NFIB small business optimism index falls to 97.9, below the 98.2 forecast and down from 98.7
squawks.detail: The NFIB small business optimism index for the US came in at 97.9. That was below the forecast of 98.2 and the previous reading of 98.7.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says intelligence-sharing cooperation with the US is continuing
squawks.detail: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha said Ukraine is still cooperating with the US on intelligence sharing. Earlier, the Kremlin said it had no knowledge of a Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv.

squawks.headline: BoK's Shin says the won has strengthened markedly on tighter policy and sees room for further gains
squawks.detail: Bank of Korea Governor Shin said the won has risen substantially because of tighter policy and that there is more scope for it to appreciate. He also said the BoK will review how its K-dot plot system has worked, with the review due next year or later.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says EU sanctions could obstruct the US-Russia fuel deal and it has no knowledge of Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said EU sanctions and other EU measures could hinder implementation of the fuel agreement between Russia and the US. He also said the Kremlin was not aware of plans by Trump to stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

squawks.headline: ECB opposes Finland's proposal to give bank supervisors a growth objective
squawks.detail: The European Central Bank has criticised a Finnish proposal that would require banking supervisors to target economic growth, according to a market news headline.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says contacts continue on Trump's energy ceasefire and sees no link between the US diesel deal and its Ukraine peace stance
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Moscow still has nothing to say about what Trump called an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, but contacts on it are ongoing. He called European criticism of the US-Russia diesel deal cynical because EU states actively buy Russian oil, and said Russia will keep selling energy on global markets.

squawks.headline: German 5-year Bobl auction sells at 3.22% yield, down from 3.28%, with bid-to-cover of 1.1 against 1.2 previously
squawks.detail: The German 5-year Bobl auction gave an average yield of 3.22%, compared with 3.28% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.1, down from 1.2.

squawks.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine has not struck Russian energy facilities for two days
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Ukraine has carried out no strikes on Russian energy targets for two days, amid the running US-brokered energy ceasefire story. He also said allies had not given warning of Russia's latest missile strike.

squawks.headline: Chancellor will not lift capital gains tax to match income tax rates, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK Chancellor has ruled out raising capital gains tax to the same level as income tax ahead of the Budget.

squawks.headline: IMF's UK growth upgrade of 0.5ppts is the joint largest in the G7, alongside Germany, Resolution Foundation notes
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the UK economy has grown faster than forecast this year, and that the IMF's upgrade to UK growth this morning was 0.5 percentage points. It says only Germany received an upgrade as large among G7 economies.

squawks.headline: BoJ reportedly unlikely to raise rates again at its October meeting
squawks.detail: A market newswire post reports that the Bank of Japan is unlikely to raise interest rates again in October. No source or further detail was given.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation publishes its UK Budget preview report, titled 'Hitting the buffers'
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation released its Budget preview and is holding a launch event this morning. Its summary points to higher inflation from the Middle East conflict and to a retreat from sovereign debt that has raised borrowing costs.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says higher yields are partly doing the Fed's job and that Trump threatens Fed independence but is not succeeding
squawks.detail: In further remarks, Federal Reserve Governor Waller said rising bond yields were doing some of the Fed's tightening work. He also said President Trump poses a threat to Fed independence but has not succeeded so far, and that he trusts Congress and the courts to protect it.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says US government bonds no longer carry a safety premium
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said the safety premium on US government bonds has disappeared. No market reaction was reported in the post.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller links the level of real yields to the effect of real growth
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said real yields are being driven by real economic growth. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says AI could help widen GDP per capita
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said artificial intelligence could add to growth in GDP per capita. The report gave no remarks on the rate outlook.

squawks.headline: IMF 2026 forecasts put UK growth joint-2nd fastest in G7 on annual average, but 6th of 7 per capita
squawks.detail: Based on the IMF's 2026 forecasts, the UK ranks joint-2nd in the G7 for annual average GDP growth, 3rd on a Q4/Q4 basis and 6th of 7 for per capita growth. A separate headline reports that UK growth has been upgraded but that energy prices and interest rates will weigh in 2027.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen condemns escalation in the Black Sea as a new front in Russia's war in Ukraine, calling it unacceptable
squawks.detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the Black Sea as another front of escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine and called it unacceptable. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US government bond funds take in almost $14bn since start of October after record $59.3bn Q3 inflows, FT says
squawks.detail: FT calculations using EPFR data show almost $14bn of inflows into US government bond funds so far in October. This follows record net inflows of $59.3bn in the third quarter.

squawks.headline: German September harmonised CPI is 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, both matching forecasts and the previous readings
squawks.detail: Germany's EU-harmonised consumer price index for September rose 3.3% on the year and 0.6% on the month. Both figures matched the 3.3% and 0.6% estimates and were unchanged from the previous readings.

squawks.headline: German final CPI confirmed at 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, both in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: Germany's final consumer price index reading shows inflation at 3.3% year on year, matching both the forecast and the previous figure of 3.3%. The monthly rise is 0.6%, also in line with the forecast and the previous reading.

squawks.headline: Banking regulators step up scrutiny of AI risks amid financial stability concerns, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters cites six people familiar with the matter as saying banking watchdogs are increasing efforts to contain AI-related risks. Some of the sources pointed to possible cyberattacks on banks or rogue AI agents as threats to global financial stability.

squawks.headline: IMF expects the BoJ to lift rates gradually towards neutral despite a projected slowdown in Japanese growth
squawks.detail: The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday that the Bank of Japan is likely to raise interest rates step by step towards a neutral setting, even though it expects Japan's growth to slow, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Dutch CPI rises 3.4% y/y in September, in line with forecast and up from 3.3%; 0.1% m/m
squawks.detail: Dutch consumer prices rose 3.4% on the year, matching the 3.4% forecast, after 3.3% previously. On the month, prices rose 0.1%, down from 0.3% before.

squawks.headline: Dollar slips in Asian trade as oil prices ease and bond yields stabilise
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the dollar fell in Asian trading on Tuesday, after a holiday in some US markets, as bond yields and oil prices eased and global stocks slid. The report gives no figures.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says core inflation is gradually nearing 2% and the BoJ is watching the bond market closely
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said inflation needs to stay anchored around the 2% target and that long-term bond yields are normally set by markets and reflect several factors.

squawks.headline: BoJ survey shows Japanese households expect prices to rise 11.8% on average over the next year, with a 10% median
squawks.detail: The figures come from the Bank of Japan's household survey on expected price changes over the year ahead.

squawks.headline: IMF warns against market complacency, naming an AI-led selloff and rising government bond yields as risks
squawks.detail: The IMF named a reversal in AI-related investment, rising government bond yields and cyberattacks as threats to financial markets, and its officials said an AI correction could hit the real economy by eroding wealth.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says the MPC must act before second-round inflation effects set in and calls UK policy still relatively accommodative
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said the risk of acting too late on inflation outweighs the risk of raising rates too early, and that the latest IMF outlook for the UK was not a surprise.

squawks.headline: IMF chief economist Tenreyro says the UK should keep to its deficit reduction plans
squawks.detail: IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro made the remarks as the Fund published its updated World Economic Outlook at its annual meetings in Bangkok.

squawks.headline: IMF raises 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.0% and warns top economies face their biggest deficits since Covid
squawks.detail: The IMF's World Economic Outlook says AI investment is offsetting energy-price shocks. It keeps its 2027 global forecast at 3.4% and sees advanced-economy growth at 2.1% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. The Fund calls for urgent action to rebuild public finances, and chief economist Tenreyro urges highly indebted countries to start fiscal consolidation.
